source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public 2:1 binds Hebrew 1:18; public 2:2–18 binds Hebrew 2:1–17. Other selected verses bind matching labels.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keep royal consolidation and divine presence as distinct opening claims.
verses.before: Solomon son of David strengthened himself over his kingdom, and the LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great.
verses.after: Solomon son of David strengthened his hold on his kingdom. The LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon son of David strengthened himself over his kingdom, and the LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great.

verses.rationale: Preserve every leadership category addressed.
verses.before: Solomon spoke to all Israel—to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader in all Israel, the heads of the ancestral houses.
verses.after: Solomon spoke to all Israel: the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the judges, and every leader in Israel, the heads of ancestral houses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon spoke to all Israel—to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader in all Israel, the heads of the ancestral houses.

verses.rationale: Keep the gathering’s destination and the tent’s Mosaic provenance.
verses.before: Then Solomon and all the assembly with him went to the high place that was at Gibeon, for the tent of meeting of God was there, which Moses servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness.
verses.after: Solomon and the whole assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon. God’s tent of meeting was there, the one Moses the LORD’s servant had made in the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Solomon and all the assembly with him went to the high place that was at Gibeon, for the tent of meeting of God was there, which Moses servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Distinguish the ark’s tent in Jerusalem from the tent at Gibeon.
verses.before: Yet David had brought up the ark of God from Kiriath-Jearim to the place David had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
verses.after: David, however, had brought God’s ark up from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: But David had brought up the ark of God from Kiriath-Jearim to the place David had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Choose the LORD as the object of seeking while noting that the pronoun may refer to the altar.
verses.before: The bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made was there before the tabernacle of the LORD, and Solomon and the assembly sought him there.
verses.after: The bronze altar made by Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, stood before the LORD’s tabernacle. Solomon and the assembly sought the LORD there.
verses.tsw_comparator: The bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made was there before the tabernacle of the LORD, and Solomon and the assembly sought him there.

verses.rationale: Retain the exact offering count and altar setting.
verses.before: Solomon went up there to the bronze altar before the LORD, which was at the tent of meeting, and offered upon it one thousand burnt offerings.
verses.after: Solomon went up there to the bronze altar before the LORD at the tent of meeting and presented a thousand burnt offerings on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon went up there to the bronze altar before the LORD, which was at the tent of meeting, and offered upon it one thousand burnt offerings.

verses.rationale: Preserve appearance without adding Kings’ dream terminology.
verses.before: That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, “Ask what I will give you.”
verses.after: That night God appeared to Solomon and said, “Ask what I should give you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, “Ask what I shall give you.”

verses.rationale: Keep faithful love connected to succession.
verses.before: Solomon said to God, “You showed great steadfast love to David my father and have made me king in his place.
verses.after: Solomon said to God, “You have shown great faithful love to my father David and have made me king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon said to God, “You showed great steadfast love to David my father and have made me king in his place.

verses.rationale: Preserve the promise and dust image.
verses.before: And now, O LORD God, let your word to David my father be confirmed, for you have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
verses.after: Now, LORD God, let your word to my father David stand firm. You have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, O LORD God, let your word to David my father be confirmed, for you have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.

verses.rationale: Retain the leadership movement image and both wisdom terms.
verses.before: Now give me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may go out and come in before this people, for who can judge this great people of yours?”
verses.after: Give me wisdom and knowledge so I can go out and come in before this people. For who can govern this great people of yours?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now give me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may go out and come in before this people, for who can judge this great people of yours?”

verses.rationale: Keep every unrequested benefit and the motive stated by God.
verses.before: God said to Solomon, “Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for riches, possessions, honor, the life of people who hate you, or even many days, but asked for yourself wisdom and knowledge so that you may judge my people over whom I have made you king,
verses.after: God said to Solomon, “Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for wealth, possessions, honor, the lives of those who hate you, or even many years of life, but asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern my people over whom I made you king,
verses.tsw_comparator: God said to Solomon, “Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for riches, possessions, honor, the life of those who hate you, or even many days, but asked for yourself wisdom and knowledge so that you may judge my people over whom I have made you king,

verses.rationale: Preserve the granted request and the additional unparalleled gifts.
verses.before: wisdom and knowledge are given to you. I will also give you riches, possessions, and honor such as no kings before you have had and none after you will have.”
verses.after: wisdom and knowledge are given to you. I will also give you wealth, possessions, and honor such as no king before you has had and none after you will have.”
verses.tsw_comparator: wisdom and knowledge are given to you. I will also give you riches, possessions, and honor such as no kings before you have had and none after you will have.”

verses.rationale: Render the difficult directional wording according to the departure context and note the Hebrew problem.
verses.before: So Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, to Jerusalem, and he reigned over Israel.
verses.after: Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, to Jerusalem, and he reigned over Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, to Jerusalem, and he reigned over Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep both totals and both stationing locations.
verses.before: Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.after: Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, which he stationed in the chariot towns and with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retain both metals and both abundance comparisons.
verses.before: The king made silver and gold in Jerusalem as common as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore trees in the foothills.
verses.after: The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as plentiful as the sycamore figs in the foothills.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king made silver and gold in Jerusalem as common as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore trees in the foothills.

verses.rationale: Choose the place-name Kue while flagging the alternative understanding of the difficult trade term.
verses.before: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; the king’s merchants purchased them from Kue at the current price.
verses.after: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue. The king’s merchants bought them from Kue at the going price.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; the king’s merchants purchased them from Kue at the current price.

verses.rationale: Supply the customary silver unit and preserve both prices and export destinations.
verses.before: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for one hundred fifty. So through them they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
verses.after: They imported a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred fifty. Through these merchants they also exported them to all the Hittite and Aramean kings.
verses.tsw_comparator: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for one hundred fifty. So through them they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.

verses.rationale: Bind this public verse to Hebrew 1:18 and retain the paired houses.
verses.before: Solomon commanded that a house be built for the name of the LORD and a royal house for himself.
verses.after: Solomon decided to build a house for the LORD’s name and a house for his own kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon commanded that a house be built for the name of the LORD and a royal house for himself.

verses.rationale: Bind Hebrew 2:1 and preserve all three workforce figures.
verses.before: Solomon counted seventy thousand burden-bearers, eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them.
verses.after: He counted out seventy thousand men to carry loads, eighty thousand to quarry stone in the hills, and thirty-six hundred to supervise them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon counted seventy thousand burden-bearers, eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them.

verses.rationale: Supply the request implicit in the comparison while retaining the earlier relationship.
verses.before: Solomon sent word to Huram king of Tyre, saying, “As you dealt with David my father and sent him cedars to build for himself a house to live in, so deal with me.
verses.after: Solomon sent this message to Huram king of Tyre: “Deal with me as you did with my father David, when you sent him cedar to build a house to live in.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon sent word to Huram king of Tyre, saying, “As you dealt with David my father and sent him cedars to build for himself a house to live in, so deal with me.

verses.rationale: Keep all worship actions, calendar occasions, and permanence.
verses.before: Look, I am building a house for the name of the LORD my God, to consecrate it to him, to burn fragrant incense before him, for the continual arrangement of bread, and for burnt offerings morning and evening, on Sabbaths, new moons, and appointed festivals of the LORD our God. This is upon Israel forever.
verses.after: I am building a house for the name of the LORD my God, to dedicate it to him: to burn fragrant incense before him, to set out bread continually, and to present burnt offerings morning and evening, on Sabbaths, new moons, and the appointed festivals of the LORD our God. This is Israel’s lasting obligation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am building a house for the name of the LORD my God, to consecrate it to him, to burn fragrant incense before him, for the continual arrangement of bread, and for burnt offerings morning and evening, on Sabbaths, new moons, and appointed festivals of the LORD our God. This is upon Israel forever.

verses.rationale: Preserve Solomon’s comparison and architectural conclusion.
verses.before: The house that I am building is great, for our God is greater than all gods.
verses.after: The house I am building will be great, because our God is greater than all gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: The house that I am building is great, for our God is greater than all gods.

verses.rationale: Keep the rhetorical limits on the temple’s ability to contain God.
verses.before: But who can build him a house, since the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain him? And who am I that I should build him a house except as a place to burn offerings before him?
verses.after: But who has the strength to build him a house? Even heaven and the highest heavens cannot contain him. Who am I to build him a house, except as a place to burn offerings before him?
verses.tsw_comparator: But who is able to build him a house, since the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain him? And who am I that I should build him a house except as a place to burn offerings before him?

verses.rationale: Preserve every material and both groups of workers.
verses.before: And now send me a skilled man to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, purple, crimson, and blue yarn, and one who knows how to engrave, to work with the skilled men who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom David my father prepared.
verses.after: Now send me a man skilled in working with gold, silver, bronze, iron, purple, crimson, and blue fabrics, and skilled in engraving. He will work with the skilled workers my father David provided for me in Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now send me a skilled man to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, purple, crimson, and blue yarn, and one who knows how to engrave, to work with the skilled men who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom David my father prepared.

verses.rationale: Keep all three tree terms and the joint workforce, continuing the purpose into the next verse.
verses.before: Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut timber from Lebanon. My servants will be with your servants,
verses.after: Send me cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon. I know your servants are skilled at cutting Lebanon’s timber. My servants will work with yours
verses.tsw_comparator: Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut timber from Lebanon. My servants will be with your servants,

verses.rationale: Retain the scale and stated reason for abundant timber.
verses.before: to prepare timber for me in abundance, for the house I am building will be great and wonderful.
verses.after: to prepare timber for me in abundance, because the house I am building will be great and extraordinary.
verses.tsw_comparator: to prepare timber for me in abundance, for the house I am building will be great and wonderful.

verses.rationale: Preserve all four equal quantities, distinct measures, and the difficult beaten-wheat description.
verses.before: Look, I will give to your servants, the woodcutters who cut the timber, twenty thousand cors of crushed wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.”
verses.after: I will give your servants, the woodcutters who fell the trees, twenty thousand cors of beaten wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I will give to your servants, the woodcutters who cut the timber, twenty thousand cors of crushed wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.”

verses.rationale: Keep the written medium and the people-centered explanation.
verses.before: Huram king of Tyre answered in a letter and sent to Solomon: “Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you king over them.”
verses.after: Huram king of Tyre replied in a letter sent to Solomon: “Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you their king.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Huram king of Tyre answered in a letter and sent to Solomon: “Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you king over them.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the foreign king’s blessing and the repeated two-house project.
verses.before: Huram said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth, who has given to David the king a wise son, endowed with discretion and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a royal house for himself.
verses.after: Huram also said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth! He has given King David a wise son with insight and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a house for his own kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: Huram said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth, who has given to David the king a wise son, endowed with discretion and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a royal house for himself.

verses.rationale: Retain the craftsman’s name-title and distinguish him from the king.
verses.before: And now I am sending a skilled and understanding man, Huram-Abi,
verses.after: I am sending Huram-abi, a skilled man with understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now I am sending a skilled and understanding man, Huram-Abi,

verses.rationale: Keep Dan rather than harmonizing Kings and preserve the full skills inventory.
verses.before: son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre. He knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, wood, purple, blue, fine linen, and crimson, and to make every kind of engraving and devise every design that may be given to him, with your skilled men and the skilled men of my lord David your father.
verses.after: His mother is from the daughters of Dan, and his father is a man of Tyre. He knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, wood, purple, blue, fine linen, and crimson, and how to do every kind of engraving and devise any design assigned to him. He will work with your skilled workers and those of my lord David your father.
verses.tsw_comparator: son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre. He knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, wood, purple, blue, fine linen, and crimson, and to make every kind of engraving and devise every design that may be given to him, with your skilled men and the skilled men of my lord David your father.

verses.rationale: Retain all four provisions in the reply’s order.
verses.before: Now therefore let my lord send to his servants the wheat, barley, oil, and wine of which he spoke,
verses.after: Now let my lord send his servants the wheat, barley, oil, and wine he promised.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore let my lord send to his servants the wheat, barley, oil, and wine of which he spoke,

verses.rationale: Preserve the sea route, named port, and division of transport responsibility.
verses.before: and we will cut timber from Lebanon according to all your need and bring it to you as rafts by sea to Joppa. Then you will bring it up to Jerusalem.”
verses.after: We will cut as much timber from Lebanon as you need and bring it to you by sea in rafts to Joppa. You can take it up to Jerusalem.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and we will cut timber from Lebanon according to all your need and bring it to you as rafts by sea to Joppa. Then you shall bring it up to Jerusalem.”

verses.rationale: Keep the counted population and exact total without presenting the labor as voluntary.
verses.before: Solomon counted all the resident aliens who were in the land of Israel after the census that David his father had taken of them, and one hundred fifty-three thousand six hundred were found.
verses.after: Solomon counted all the foreign men living in the land of Israel, following the count his father David had made. There were 153,600.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon counted all the resident aliens who were in the land of Israel after the census that David his father had taken of them, and one hundred fifty-three thousand six hundred were found.

verses.rationale: Retain every assignment and the coercive force of making the people work.
verses.before: He appointed seventy thousand of them as burden-bearers, eighty thousand as stonecutters in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred as overseers to make the people work.
verses.after: He assigned seventy thousand of them to carry loads, eighty thousand to quarry stone in the hills, and thirty-six hundred as supervisors to keep the people at work.
verses.tsw_comparator: He appointed seventy thousand of them as burden-bearers, eighty thousand as stonecutters in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred as overseers to make the people work.

verses.rationale: Supply the LORD as the appearance’s subject and preserve the full site identification.
verses.before: Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to David his father, at the place David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.after: Solomon began building the LORD’s house in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David, at the place David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to David his father, at the place David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

verses.rationale: Supply day for the elliptical second and retain all date elements.
verses.before: He began to build on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
verses.after: He began building on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign.
verses.tsw_comparator: He began to build on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.

verses.rationale: Keep the older cubit standard and both foundation dimensions.
verses.before: These are the foundations Solomon laid for building the house of God: the length in cubits according to the former measure was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
verses.after: These were the foundation dimensions Solomon used for building God’s house, measured in cubits of the older standard: sixty cubits long and twenty cubits wide.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the foundations Solomon laid for building the house of God: the length in cubits according to the former measure was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.

verses.rationale: Retain the Hebrew’s striking height and flag the twenty-cubit alternative without silently correcting it.
verses.before: The porch that was in front of the house was twenty cubits long, corresponding to the width of the house, and its height was one hundred twenty cubits. He overlaid its interior with pure gold.
verses.after: The entrance hall across the front was twenty cubits long, matching the width of the house, and a hundred twenty cubits high. He overlaid its interior with pure gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: The porch that was in front of the house was twenty cubits long, corresponding to the width of the house, and its height was one hundred twenty cubits. He overlaid its interior with pure gold.

verses.rationale: Preserve the underlying wood, gold covering, and both decorative motifs.
verses.before: The great house he paneled with cypress wood, overlaid it with fine gold, and put palm trees and chains upon it.
verses.after: He paneled the main hall with cypress, overlaid it with fine gold, and decorated it with palm trees and chains.
verses.tsw_comparator: The great house he paneled with cypress wood, overlaid it with fine gold, and put palm trees and chains upon it.

verses.rationale: Keep the ornamental purpose and uncertain gold provenance.
verses.before: He adorned the house with precious stones for beauty, and the gold was gold from Parvaim.
verses.after: He adorned the house with precious stones for beauty. The gold was gold from Parvaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: He adorned the house with precious stones for beauty, and the gold was gold from Parvaim.

verses.rationale: Retain all structural elements and carved creatures.
verses.before: He overlaid the house—the beams, thresholds, walls, and doors—with gold and carved cherubim on the walls.
verses.after: He overlaid the house—its beams, thresholds, walls, and doors—with gold, and carved cherubim on the walls.
verses.tsw_comparator: He overlaid the house—the beams, thresholds, walls, and doors—with gold and carved cherubim on the walls.

verses.rationale: Keep the square dimensions and large gold weight.
verses.before: He made the house of the Most Holy Place. Its length corresponded to the width of the house, twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits. He overlaid it with six hundred talents of fine gold.
verses.after: He made the Most Holy Place twenty cubits long, across the width of the house, and twenty cubits wide. He overlaid it with six hundred talents of fine gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the house of the Most Holy Place. Its length corresponded to the width of the house, twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits. He overlaid it with six hundred talents of fine gold.

verses.rationale: Retain the stated aggregate weight without asserting each nail weighed fifty.
verses.before: The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold, and he overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
verses.after: The gold nails weighed fifty shekels. He also overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold, and he overlaid the upper rooms with gold.

verses.rationale: Preserve two figures and the uncertain workmanship term at a general level.
verses.before: In the house of the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of sculptured work and overlaid them with gold.
verses.after: In the Most Holy Place he made two sculpted cherubim and overlaid them with gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the house of the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of sculptured work and overlaid them with gold.

verses.rationale: Keep the total span and the first figure’s two contacts.
verses.before: The wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits long. One wing of the first cherub was five cubits and touched the wall of the house, and its other wing was five cubits and touched the wing of the other cherub.
verses.after: Together the cherubim’s wings spanned twenty cubits. One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long and touched the wall of the house; its other wing was five cubits long and touched the other cherub’s wing.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits long. One wing of the first cherub was five cubits and touched the wall of the house, and its other wing was five cubits and touched the wing of the other cherub.

verses.rationale: Preserve the mirrored geometry and each five-cubit wing.
verses.before: One wing of the second cherub was five cubits and touched the wall of the house, and its other wing was five cubits and joined the wing of the first cherub.
verses.after: One wing of the other cherub was five cubits long and touched the other wall of the house; its other wing was five cubits long and joined the first cherub’s wing.
verses.tsw_comparator: One wing of the second cherub was five cubits and touched the wall of the house, and its other wing was five cubits and joined the wing of the first cherub.

verses.rationale: Keep standing posture and the outward-facing direction.
verses.before: The wings of these cherubim spread out twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, and their faces were toward the house.
verses.after: The wings of these cherubim spread out twenty cubits. The cherubim stood on their feet, facing the main hall.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wings of these cherubim spread out twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, and their faces were toward the house.

verses.rationale: Retain every textile color and the woven imagery.
verses.before: He made the curtain of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen and worked cherubim into it.
verses.after: He made the curtain of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, and worked cherubim into it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the curtain of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen and worked cherubim into it.

verses.rationale: Keep thirty-five without adding each or combined where the Hebrew does not settle it.
verses.before: In front of the house he made two pillars thirty-five cubits high, and the capital on top of each was five cubits.
verses.after: He made two pillars in front of the house, thirty-five cubits in length, with a capital five cubits high on top of each.
verses.tsw_comparator: In front of the house he made two pillars thirty-five cubits high, and the capital on top of each was five cubits.

verses.rationale: Retain the difficult inner-sanctuary wording and exact pomegranate count, with the alternative noted.
verses.before: He made chains in the inner sanctuary and put them on the tops of the pillars, and he made one hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.
verses.after: He made chains in the inner sanctuary and placed them on top of the pillars. He made a hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made chains in the inner sanctuary and put them on the tops of the pillars, and he made one hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.

verses.rationale: Keep both relative positions and meaningful pillar names.
verses.before: He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and one on the left. He called the name of the one on the right Jachin and the name of the one on the left Boaz.
verses.after: He erected the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and one on the left. He named the right one Jachin and the left one Boaz.
verses.tsw_comparator: He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and one on the left. He called the name of the one on the right Jachin and the name of the one on the left Boaz.

verses.rationale: Preserve all three altar dimensions.
verses.before: He made a bronze altar, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high.
verses.after: He made a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made a bronze altar, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high.

verses.rationale: Keep the named Sea and the source’s diameter, height, and circumference without recalculating them.
verses.before: He made the Sea of cast metal, ten cubits from rim to rim, circular all around, five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits encircled it.
verses.after: He made the Sea of cast metal, round in shape, ten cubits from rim to rim and five cubits high. A measuring line thirty cubits long encircled it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the Sea of cast metal, ten cubits from rim to rim, circular all around, five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits encircled it.

verses.rationale: Retain oxen rather than substituting Kings’ gourds and preserve the casting method.
verses.before: Under it were figures of oxen all around, ten to a cubit, encircling the Sea all around. The oxen were in two rows, cast as one piece with it.
verses.after: Figures of oxen encircled it underneath, ten to a cubit, all around the Sea. The oxen were in two rows, cast in one piece with it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Under it were figures of oxen all around, ten to a cubit, encircling the Sea all around. The oxen were in two rows, cast as one piece with it.

verses.rationale: Keep every orientation and the inward-facing rear portions.
verses.before: It stood upon twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea was set upon them, and all their hindquarters were inward.
verses.after: It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three west, three south, and three east. The Sea rested above them, and all their hindquarters faced inward.
verses.tsw_comparator: It stood upon twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea was set upon them, and all their hindquarters were inward.

verses.rationale: Retain thickness, both shape comparisons, and Chronicles’ three-thousand capacity.
verses.before: Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its rim was made like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held three thousand baths.
verses.after: It was a handbreadth thick. Its rim was shaped like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold three thousand baths.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its rim was made like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held three thousand baths.

verses.rationale: Distinguish sacrificial washing from priestly washing and preserve the five-plus-five arrangement.
verses.before: He made ten basins and put five on the right and five on the left to wash in them. The things used for the burnt offering were rinsed in them, but the Sea was for the priests to wash in.
verses.after: He made ten basins, placing five on the right and five on the left, for washing. They rinsed the materials for the burnt offering in them, while the Sea was for the priests to wash in.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made ten basins and put five on the right and five on the left to wash in them. The things used for the burnt offering were rinsed in them, but the Sea was for the priests to wash in.

verses.rationale: Keep the design reference and symmetrical placement.
verses.before: He made ten gold lampstands according to their design and set them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.
verses.after: He made ten gold lampstands according to their prescribed design and put them in the main hall, five on the right and five on the left.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made ten gold lampstands according to their design and set them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.

verses.rationale: Retain both furnishing counts and table positions.
verses.before: He made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. He also made one hundred gold bowls.
verses.after: He made ten tables and put them in the main hall, five on the right and five on the left. He also made a hundred gold sprinkling bowls.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. He also made one hundred gold bowls.

verses.rationale: Preserve the two courts and door covering.
verses.before: He made the court of the priests and the great court and doors for the court, and overlaid their doors with bronze.
verses.after: He made the priests’ courtyard, the great courtyard, and doors for the courtyard, and overlaid the doors with bronze.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the court of the priests and the great court and doors for the court, and overlaid their doors with bronze.

verses.rationale: Unfold the east-and-south orientation concisely while retaining right side.
verses.before: He set the Sea on the right side, toward the southeast.
verses.after: He placed the Sea on the right side, toward the southeast.
verses.tsw_comparator: He set the Sea on the right side, toward the southeast.

verses.rationale: Follow Huram’s read form and introduce the concluding inventory.
verses.before: Huram made the pots, shovels, and bowls. So Huram finished doing the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of God:
verses.after: Huram made the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. So Huram finished the work he did for King Solomon in God’s house:
verses.tsw_comparator: Huram made the pots, shovels, and bowls. So Huram finished doing the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of God:

verses.rationale: Preserve the nested two-part architectural inventory.
verses.before: the two pillars, the bowls of the capitals that were on top of the two pillars, the two networks covering the two bowls of the capitals that were on top of the pillars,
verses.after: the two pillars, the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars, and the two networks covering the two bowl-shaped capitals;
verses.tsw_comparator: the two pillars, the bowls of the capitals that were on top of the two pillars, the two networks covering the two bowls of the capitals that were on top of the pillars,

verses.rationale: Retain the four-hundred total and two rows on each network.
verses.before: the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were upon the pillars.
verses.after: the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network covering the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;
verses.tsw_comparator: the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were upon the pillars.

verses.rationale: Keep both supporting and supported furnishings.
verses.before: He made the stands, and he made the basins upon the stands,
verses.after: the stands and the basins he made on the stands;
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the stands, and he made the basins upon the stands,

verses.rationale: Preserve the singular Sea and twelve supports.
verses.before: the one Sea and the twelve oxen beneath it,
verses.after: the one Sea and the twelve oxen beneath it;
verses.tsw_comparator: the one Sea and the twelve oxen beneath it,

verses.rationale: Keep all utensil categories, the craftsman’s title, and the polished metal.
verses.before: the pots, shovels, forks, and all their equipment. Huram-Abiv made them for King Solomon for the house of the LORD from polished bronze.
verses.after: and the pots, shovels, forks, and all their utensils. Huram-abi made these of polished bronze for King Solomon for the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: the pots, shovels, forks, and all their equipment. Huram-Abiv made them for King Solomon for the house of the LORD from polished bronze.

verses.rationale: Retain the casting location and Chronicles’ Zeredah name.
verses.before: The king cast them in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
verses.after: The king had them cast in the clay ground of the Jordan plain, between Succoth and Zeredah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king cast them in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.

verses.rationale: Keep the abundance and unmeasured weight without inventing an amount.
verses.before: Solomon made all these vessels in very great abundance, for the weight of the bronze was not determined.
verses.after: Solomon made all these utensils in such great quantities that the weight of the bronze was never determined.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon made all these vessels in very great abundance, for the weight of the bronze was not determined.

verses.rationale: Retain the gold altar and the distinctive bread name.
verses.before: Solomon made all the vessels that were in the house of God: the gold altar, the tables upon which was the bread of the Presence,
verses.after: Solomon also made all the furnishings for God’s house: the gold altar, the tables on which the bread of the Presence was placed,
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon made all the vessels that were in the house of God: the gold altar, the tables upon which was the bread of the Presence,

verses.rationale: Keep material, purpose, and sanctuary location.
verses.before: the lampstands and their lamps of pure gold, to burn according to the ordinance before the inner sanctuary,
verses.after: the lampstands and their lamps of pure gold, to burn as prescribed before the inner sanctuary,
verses.tsw_comparator: the lampstands and their lamps of pure gold, to burn according to the ordinance before the inner sanctuary,

verses.rationale: Preserve all three items and the emphatic purity statement.
verses.before: the flowers, lamps, and tongs of gold, of the finest gold,
verses.after: the flowers, lamps, and tongs of gold—the purest gold—
verses.tsw_comparator: the flowers, lamps, and tongs of gold, of the finest gold,

verses.rationale: Keep all remaining utensils and both sets of doors.
verses.before: the snuffers, bowls, dishes, and firepans of pure gold, and the entrance of the house—its inner doors to the Most Holy Place and the doors of the house of the temple—of gold.
verses.after: and the wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes, and firepans of pure gold. The entrances of the house—the inner doors to the Most Holy Place and the doors to the main hall—were gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: the snuffers, bowls, dishes, and firepans of pure gold, and the entrance of the house—its inner doors to the Most Holy Place and the doors of the house of the temple—of gold.

verses.rationale: Preserve completion and the continuity with David’s gifts.
verses.before: Thus all the work that Solomon did for the house of the LORD was finished. Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father—the silver, the gold, and all the vessels—and put them in the treasuries of the house of God.
verses.after: When all Solomon’s work for the LORD’s house was finished, he brought in the things his father David had dedicated. He placed the silver, gold, and all the utensils in the treasuries of God’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus all the work that Solomon did for the house of the LORD was finished. Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father—the silver, the gold, and all the vessels—and put them in the treasuries of the house of God.

verses.rationale: Keep every leadership group and identify Zion without conflating the two locations.
verses.before: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the children of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the city of David, which is Zion.
verses.after: Then Solomon assembled Israel’s elders, all the tribal heads, and the leaders of the Israelite ancestral houses in Jerusalem, to bring the ark of the LORD’s covenant up from the City of David, that is, Zion.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the children of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the city of David, which is Zion.

verses.rationale: Preserve the male referent and the unnamed festival’s timing.
verses.before: All the men of Israel assembled to the king at the festival, which was in the seventh month.
verses.after: All the men of Israel assembled before the king at the festival in the seventh month.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the men of Israel assembled to the king at the festival, which was in the seventh month.

verses.rationale: Keep Levites as carriers here before the priests’ role in verse 7.
verses.before: All the elders of Israel came, and the Levites carried the ark.
verses.after: All Israel’s elders came, and the Levites lifted the ark.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the elders of Israel came, and the Levites carried the ark.

verses.rationale: Render the adjacent priests-Levites phrase as Levitical priests while noting the alternative priests and Levites.
verses.before: They brought up the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent. The Levitical priests brought them up.
verses.after: They brought up the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy utensils in the tent. The Levitical priests brought them up.
verses.tsw_comparator: They brought up the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent. The Levitical priests brought them up.

verses.rationale: Retain both counting terms and the unquantified abundance.
verses.before: King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel assembled before him were sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted or numbered for multitude.
verses.after: King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel gathered with him before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that they could not be counted or numbered.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel assembled before him were sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted or numbered for multitude.

verses.rationale: Preserve the nested location and the priests as carriers into it.
verses.before: The priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, to the inner sanctuary of the house, to the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
verses.after: The priests brought the ark of the LORD’s covenant to its place in the inner sanctuary of the house, the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, to the inner sanctuary of the house, to the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.

verses.rationale: Keep both objects sheltered by the wings.
verses.before: For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles from above.
verses.after: The cherubim spread their wings over the ark’s place, covering the ark and its poles from above.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles from above.

verses.rationale: Retain the difficult from-the-ark wording and the narrator’s singular enduring referent.
verses.before: The poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the Holy Place before the inner sanctuary, but they were not seen outside. They are there to this day.
verses.after: The poles were so long that their ends could be seen extending from the ark in front of the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen from outside. It remains there to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: The poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the Holy Place before the inner sanctuary, but they were not seen outside. They are there to this day.

verses.rationale: Keep the restrictive contents statement and covenant setting.
verses.before: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses put there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the children of Israel when they came out from Egypt.
verses.after: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets Moses had placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses put there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the children of Israel when they came out from Egypt.

verses.rationale: Unfold the parenthesis as a sentence and preserve the suspension of division distinctions.
verses.before: And it happened when the priests came out from the Holy Place—for all the priests who were present had consecrated themselves without regard to their divisions—
verses.after: The priests came out of the holy place. All the priests present had consecrated themselves, without regard to their divisions.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when the priests came out from the Holy Place—for all the priests who were present had consecrated themselves without regard to their divisions—

verses.rationale: Keep the full musical personnel, dress, location, instruments, and exact priest count.
verses.before: and all the Levites who were singers, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and brothers, clothed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, stood east of the altar, and with them one hundred twenty priests blowing trumpets—
verses.after: All the Levitical singers—Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, their sons, and their relatives—stood east of the altar, dressed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres. With them were a hundred twenty priests sounding trumpets.
verses.tsw_comparator: and all the Levites who were singers, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and brothers, clothed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, stood east of the altar, and with them one hundred twenty priests blowing trumpets—

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated unity, recognizable refrain, and repeated house identification.
verses.before: and it happened when the trumpeters and singers were as one, making one voice to praise and give thanks to the LORD, and when they raised their voice with trumpets, cymbals, and instruments of song, and praised the LORD: “For he is good, for his steadfast love is forever,” then the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud.
verses.after: The trumpeters and singers joined as one, making one sound of praise and thanksgiving to the LORD. They raised their voices with trumpets, cymbals, and musical instruments, praising the LORD: “For he is good; his faithful love lasts forever.” Then a cloud filled the house, the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: and it happened when the trumpeters and singers were as one, making one voice to praise and give thanks to the LORD, and when they raised their voice with trumpets, cymbals, and instruments of song, and praised the LORD: “For he is good, for his steadfast love is forever,” then the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud.

verses.rationale: Keep the physical inability to serve and the glory filling the sanctuary.
verses.before: The priests were not able to stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.
verses.after: The priests could not remain standing to serve because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled God’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priests were not able to stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.

comparative_references.scope: All 88 TSW verses read after drafting independently from every pinned Hebrew verse and its source notes.
